relation.rationale: At n=2 the general layer-mean and independent-environment floor is H_2=3/2; the witness computes the remaining centered variance and entire OU overlap explicitly.

from_statement: AUTHOR-DERIVED, UNREVIEWED exact finite witness. In the independent standard-Gaussian quadrant polymer with two vertices per path, the two paths share the origin and choose either (1,0) or (0,1). M_2=g_0+max(g_1,g_2). With OU time t>=0 and g_t=e^(-t)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))g' for independent g', the expected number of shared maximizing-path vertices is R_2(t)=3/2+arcsin(e^(-t))/pi, and Var(M_2)=2-1/pi. Thus R_2(t)>=3/2 and its independent-environment limit is 3/2. A bound R_2(t)<=C exp(-c t) for all t with finite C and c>0 is false. Centered-overlap estimates must also account for the first-chaos variance floor. This is a proof-step counterexample, not a disproof of polynomial variance improvement.
to_statement: AUTHOR-DERIVED, UNREVIEWED finite-n identities. Let M_n=max_p sum_{v in p}g_v for n-vertex up/right paths from the origin in Z_+^2 with free endpoint and independent N(0,1) vertex weights. Define A_i as the mean of the i+1 weights on x+y=i, r_v=g_v-A_i on that layer, and H_n=sum_{j=1}^n 1/j. The layer means are Gaussian-independent of r, and M_n(g)=sum_{i=0}^{n-1}A_i+M_n(r), so Var(M_n)=H_n+Var(M_n(r)). For F_{n,beta}=log sum_p exp(beta sum_{v in p}g_v) at fixed beta>0, Var(F_{n,beta})=beta^2 H_n+Var(F_{n,beta}(r)). Under OU coupling g_t=e^(-t)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))g', maximizing-path overlap R_n(t) has floor sum_v P(v in P_n)^2>=H_n at every t>=0. These identities do not establish a power variance upper bound.
